extracted.intended_audience: grant peer reviewers, funding panelists, program officers, and researchers studying peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Operationalisation of the NSF 'mail reviewer' evaluation form and related panel norms: reviewers rate proposals on multiple dimensions (5‑point scale) and supply written justification, and panels should use multiple reviewers and procedural safeguards to manage low inter-rater reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probable scientific significance / importance of the proposed research
rubrics_metrics.description: Would the work, if successful, advance the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated on a 5-point scale (Excellent / Very Good / Good / Fair / Poor); reviewers should supply a written justification explaining why the project would or would not advance the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of the research
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it open new ground rather than incremental refinement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated on the 5-point scale; reviewers should note whether the proposal represents novel conceptual or methodological contributions versus incremental work, and justify their assessment in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of the research design / methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness, feasibility, technical specification of the proposed research design and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate on the 5-point scale and provide written comments on methodological rigor, feasibility, potential pitfalls, and whether methods are appropriate to achieve stated aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific competence of the principal investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record and demonstrated ability of the PI to carry out the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate on the 5-point scale; avoid allowing prior reputation alone to determine score (see halo effect guidance). Provide concrete evidence from the PI's record that supports ability to execute the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of facilities and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional capacity and available resources to execute the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate on the 5-point scale and comment on institutional support, equipment, collaborations, and other resource constraints or strengths that affect feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of the grant on the scientific infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact of funding on training (students), instrumentation, and broader infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate on the 5-point scale; discuss expected contributions to workforce development, student training, shared facilities, or instrumentation that increase community capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall recommendation for funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorical funding recommendation using: Must Fund / Should Fund / Could Fund / Should Not Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers give an overall categorical recommendation in addition to dimension scores and must supply a written justification linking dimension assessments to the funding decision category.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5-point rating scale and written justification protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Each substantive dimension is rated on a 5-point scale (Excellent / Very Good / Good / Fair / Poor) and reviewers must supply written justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scale standardizes ordinal judgments across dimensions; written justification is required to reveal grounds of evaluation, enabling panels to diagnose disagreements and preventing undocumented summary assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise low inter-rater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical finding: the modal Pearson correlation between independent reviewers' ratings was ~0.25, indicating substantial noise in individual reviewer judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and panels should treat each review as a noisy estimate, avoid overconfidence in single reviews, and design procedures (multiple reviewers, aggregation with bounds) that account for low reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulate substantive grounds when disagreeing
rubrics_metrics.description: Disagreement among reviewers is endemic and largely substantive—reflecting genuine differences about what counts as good science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explicitly explain the substantive bases of their judgments (e.g., significance vs methodology) rather than relying on summary judgments alone, so panels can diagnose the source of disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid halo effects from PI reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Halo effects from PI reputation explain a large share of reviewer agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should explicitly try to evaluate the proposal independently of the investigator's prior eminence; panels should discount the marginal predictive value of PI reputation when the proposal itself provides informative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make explicit weighting for field heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria such as 'originality' carry different weights across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should state how they weight different dimensions for the specific discipline and justify those weightings so panels understand discipline-specific priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple independent reviewers (panel composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels should use multiple independent reviewers (recommendation: at least 4–6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using 4–6 reviewers reduces the influence of individual noise; panels should not treat the average as absolute truth but as an estimate with known reliability bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate scores by dimension for diagnostic transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Require reviewers to provide separate scores for each evaluation dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dimension-separated scores allow diagnosis of disagreement (e.g., significance vs methodology) and facilitate informed panel discussion and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat aggregated scores as reliability-bounded estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel averages are estimates subject to measurement error and should be interpreted with explicit attention to reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels should present aggregated scores alongside uncertainty or bounds (implicitly or explicitly) and avoid overinterpreting small score differences as decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise and manage the 'zone of indifference' near cut-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an inevitable 'zone of indifference' near the funding cut-off where lottery-like effects dominate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels should acknowledge when proposals fall into this zone, avoid pretending false precision, and consider procedural responses (e.g., lotteries, tie-breaking rules) rather than treating small score differentials as meaningful.
